title: Coalesce IO polymorphic workers and batched serialization to cut CPU tail latency
author: Samir Kapoor
description: Background: production telemetry shows CPU-side tails driven by frequent short-lived IO wakeups and per-request serialization overhead (small payloads, many concurrent connections). Motivation: reduce syscall churn and cache thrash without changing existing external APIs. Change summary: introduce a configurable IO coalescer that groups pending socket/FD readiness into short (<500us) micro-batches processed by polymorphic workers, unify the per-request serialization path into a batched serializer that encodes multiple response frames in one pass, and add lightweight pacing to the worker pool so CPU pinning is optional. Design goals: (1) preserve latency SLOs for single-request fast paths, (2) reduce 95/99p CPU tail by avoiding repeated thread wake/sleep, (3) keep the change runtime-configurable and safe to roll back. What this PR does: 1) new module runner/scheduler/io_coalescer.rs that aggregates readiness events per-core and dispatches grouped events to polymorphic workers; 2) polymorphic worker pool (runner/scheduler/worker_pool.rs) that supports CPU-pinned and unpinned modes and can handle small burst windows; 3) batched serializer (runtime/serialization/batch_serializer.cpp) that takes vectorized response items and applies shared formatting/kernels once; 4) lightweight KV prefetch hints in runtime/kvcache/prefetcher.py to warm hot keys observed in batched requests; 5) a new runtime flag io.coalesce_workers (default: false for safety) and debug tracing; 6) benchmarks and perf harness changes under bench/perf/coalescer/*. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked in Linear ENG-2120 | - [x] unit + integration tests added | - [x] microbench harness and CI perf job updated | - [x] feature gated behind runtime flag | - [x] rollout plan with canary and metrics tracked Performance: end-to-end lab tests (nvme-backed VM, 32 vCPU, 8x A10 equivalent inference GPUs simulated) show: baseline 95th CPU-side request path latency 48ms -> 16-20ms with coalescer+batched-serializer enabled; p99 reduced 92ms -> 36ms; average CPU cycles/request reduced ~2.8x; observed 18% drop in token-level throughput at 1000 concurrent connections due to batching-induced micro-queueing in aggressive mode (mitigated by default conservative windows). Safety and compatibility: no external API changes, no model-serving kernel modifications; kvcache prefetch is best-effort. Rollout: staged enablement via feature flag; canary in us-west with 5% traffic for 24h, then 25%, then full. Revert: set io.coalesce_workers=false and redeploy; fallback safe-path keeps original serializer and worker semantics. Related: ENG-2187 (bench regression triage), SUP-4421 (customer report of tail CPU).
commits: Add io_coalescer module and integration tests
Introduce polymorphic worker pool with optional pinning
Implement batch_serializer C++ path and unit tests
KV prefetch hinting and runtime flag
release_notes: Introduce IO coalescer and batched serializer (opt-in). Reduces CPU-side tail latency; enable via runtime flag io.coalesce_workers. See perf notes for conservative defaults.
comments_summary: Initial design + benchmark posted by author. Avery asked for deterministic timers for coalescing window and a guard for high-load no-coalesce path; author added timer meters and a short-circuit fast-path. Morgan requested metrics for micro-batch size distribution and per-worker queue depth; added histograms and dashboards. Elena flagged potential interaction with existing affinity pinning; author added polymorphic worker modes and default unpinned rollout. CI perf job rerun once after minor allocator tweak; final approval from Avery and Morgan before merge.
benchmark_summary: Lab perf: 95p CPU-side latency 48ms -> 16-20ms; p99 92ms -> 36ms; average cycles/request ~2.8x improvement; small throughput tradeoff under aggressive batching (up to -18% at extreme concurrency); mitigations and conservative defaults included.
rollback_plan: Disable runtime flag io.coalesce_workers and redeploy the control-plane config. If metrics do not recover within 15m, revert the release to previous image. All changes are gated so rollback does not require DB migration or data changes.
